defects.source_says: EO 12353 was signed March 23, 1982 (47 FR 12785; OFR note on EO 10927: 'Revoked by: EO 12353, March 23, 1982'). The clause's own judgment_reason dates the performed revocation 1982-03-23; an end three years before the order existed is wrong and internally inconsistent.

The clause carries a first_end and its judgment_reason says the revocation of EO 10927 was performed once on issuance with no continuing duty; the rationale and independent_command_check call it 'its own terminated clause'. A clause with a first end cannot be operative at the cutoff, and it has no current_predicate.

evidence_checked: OFR notes: EO 12353 Revokes EO 10927; Amended by EO 12404, EO 13743; See Cornelius v. NAACP LDF

reasons: Identity (EO 12353, March 23, 1982, 47 FR 12785), quotes and the corrected ten-clause inventory check out; the amendments by EO 12404 (1983-02-10) and EO 13743 (2016-10-13) are correctly treated as later events, and no held Revoked/Superseded note exists for the order, so the YES outcome is supported for sections 1-8 and the 9b savings sentence. The section 9 revocation clause (c9a) is defective: its first_end date is 1979-03-23, before the order was signed and contrary to its own reason (1982-03-23), and it is marked operative while carrying a first end and being described as terminated. Rejected for wrong date and internal inconsistency.
